findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can race and overwrite each other
findings.body: Removing the lock around the whole BuildIndex function leaves no per-key serialization: getOrCreateIndex does GetIndex and then BuildIndex without any lock, and BuildIndex does not re-check the cache before building. Two concurrent searches/watch events for the same NamespacedResource can therefore build two indexes. For file-backed indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory concurrently, which can fail or corrupt the index; for in-memory indexes the second build overwrites the first in the cache, so a search/watch that already got the first index keeps writing to an index the cache will never return again. Add a per-key singleflight/build lock and re-check the cache under that lock before starting a build.

findings.title: Index build goroutines race on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed
findings.body: Inside init, every errgroup goroutine assigns to the shared outer err variable and increments totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization. One goroutine can overwrite the error from another before it returns, so group.Wait may report success even when an index build failed; the count used for the span/event is also racy. Use a local err in each goroutine and an atomic or mutex-protected counter.

findings.title: Stop no longer prevents requests because handlers no longer observe initErr
findings.body: Stop sets s.initErr to a stopping/stopped error, and the per-RPC s.Init(ctx) calls used to return that error so requests arriving after shutdown failed fast. Those calls were removed without adding an equivalent stopped-state check, so Create/Update/Delete/List/Watch/Search/etc. can still execute after Stop and after lifecycle.Stop has begun closing or canceling the backend. Add an explicit stopped flag/check in the handlers or in an interceptor.

findings.title: Postgres integration test is skipped instead of fixing startup init failure
findings.body: The PR adds a skip for postgres to the storage-server integration test, with a TODO that it fails in Drone. This PR changes unified storage initialization to happen synchronously during server construction, so disabling the postgres case hides a possible regression in the new startup behavior and leaves the storage-server target without postgres integration coverage. Fix the underlying failure or add equivalent coverage before merging.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: BuildIndex now mutates b.cache under cacheMu, but TotalDocs ranges over the same map without any lock. If TotalDocs is called while an index build stores its result, this is a Go map concurrent read/write race and can panic. Take cacheMu.RLock while iterating.
